newsitem.title: USA: Indosuez to hire 300 Dean Witter futures employees.
newsitem.headline: Indosuez to hire 300 Dean Witter futures employees.

text.p: Indosuez Carr Futures Inc., a wholly owned subsidiary of Banque Indosuez, said Monday it would hire the roughly 300 employees of Dean Witter Reynolds Inc.'s institutional futures division.
This would bring the number of U.S. employees at the Chicago-based Indosuez unit to 450.

Dean Witter Reynolds, the securities business unit of Dean Witter, Discover & Co., said Sunday it sold its institutional futures business to Banque Indosuez, which itself was acquired by France's Credit Agricole in December.
"We will hire people from Dean Witter, and obviously that means we will reorganize our North American operations," said Didier Varlet, chairman of Indosuez Carr, in an interview.
The acquisition is expected to be completed by the end of June, subject to Federal Reserve Board approval, Varlet said.
About 30 percent of Dean Witter's institutional employees are concentrated in commodity or nonfinancial markets, including metals and energy, Varlet said.
Indosuez Carr, which has been a futures commission merchant since 1987, and Dean Witter have a total of 800 employees worldwide, Varlet said.
Indosuez Carr officials would not comment on the terms of the purchase and would not disclose the worth of Dean Witter's roughly 500 institutional futures accounts.
Dean Witter's sale of most of its futures business came less than a month before Dean Witter and Morgan Stanley Group Inc. are expected to close a merger worth $10.3 billion.
Indosuez Carr has operations in London, Paris, Madrid, Singapore and Tokyo, as well as in Chicago and New York, while Dean Witter operates mainly in the United States and London.
